note: The input font's CFF2 CharStrings INDEX supplies the glyph charstring bytes that will be interpreted for the glyph-extents query.
The selected input-controlled charstring is installed as the CFF2 interpreter byte stream.
The one-byte integer operand from the charstring is pushed on the argument stack and later used as the blend operand count n.
The blend operator consumes the input-controlled stack operand as n, the number of default values to blend.
The code subtracts the required number of blend operands from the current stack count without first requiring that the stack contain at least (k+1)*n values, so start can underflow.

code: env.argStack[start + i].set_blends (n, i, k, &env.argStack[start + n + (i * k)]);
note: The underflowed start index is used to form the source pointer for the blend deltas passed to set_blends.
set_blends reads BlendArg elements through the out-of-range blends_ pointer, producing the global-buffer-overflow read.
